title: Vázquez says Durandus meant only habitual grace
source_text: XII. Pertendit quidem Vasques Durandum ibi loqui, non de gratia quavis, sed solum de gratia habituali & justificante; & non putat aliquem esse Doctorem Catholicum qui docuerit hominem posse evitare omnem tentationem contra jus naturale, ac proinde servare omnem naturalem legem, non solum brevi, sed etiam longo tempore, sine ullo auxilio gratiae per Christum. Durandum enim & alios veteres Scholasticos, quum disputant de victoria tentationum, & de observatione praeceptorum naturalium, An sine gratia possit quis vincere omnes tentationes, & observare omnia praecepta; per gratiam non intelligere auxilium gratiae moventis, sed gratiam habitualem, qua justi sumus. In primam 2. tom. 2. Disput. 189. cap. 2.
pass_a_gloss: XII. Vasques indeed maintains that Durandus there speaks, not of any grace whatever, but only of habitual and justifying grace; and he does not think that there is any Catholic Doctor who taught that man can avoid every temptation against natural right, and accordingly keep all the natural law, not only for a short, but also for a long time, without any help of grace through Christ. For Durandus and other old Scholastics, when they dispute about the victory over temptations, and about the observance of the natural precepts, Whether without grace one can overcome all temptations, and observe all the precepts, by grace do not understand the help of moving grace, but habitual grace, by which we are just. On the First of the Second, tome 2, Disputation 189, chapter 2.
pass_b_english: Vázquez does maintain that Durandus is speaking there not of any grace at all but only of habitual and justifying grace. He does not think any Catholic doctor has taught that man can resist every temptation against natural law, and so keep the whole natural law, not only for a short time but for a long time too, without any help of grace through Christ.

When Durandus and the other older Schoolmen debate the overcoming of temptations and the keeping of the natural precepts, and ask whether a man can overcome all temptations and keep all the precepts without grace, by 'grace' they mean, he says, not the help of moving grace but habitual grace, by which we are righteous. On the Prima Secundae, vol. 2, disputation 189, chapter 2.
